Header:
Date: 2027-01-26 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 55 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Roberts (Marigold Head of AI), Sofia Alvarez (Infra Lead), Derek Cho (Security)

Auto Summary (auto-gen): High level POC decision leaning toward Dedicated for predictable throughput but Customer wants to validate private option due to data residency. Need benchmarks and security docs.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:06] Liam Roberts: Hey, Liam here.
[00:08] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia.
[00:10] Derek Cho: Derek.
[00:12] Ethan Patel: Ethan from Redwood.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Awesome. Agenda — go over Marigold's workload, success criteria, then deployment tradeoffs, then next steps.
[00:28] Liam Roberts: To kick off, our use case is twofold: 1) conversational claims assistant, around 120 concurrent users during bursts — average RPS per user low but spikes to 200 RPS total, and 2) nightly batch embeddings for search, about 10M docs monthly. Latency is critical for chat, we want p95 under 300 ms ideally.
[00:55] Sofia Alvarez: On infra side we care about VPC peering or private link, and keys can't leave region X, also SOC2 audit needs. We may require customer-managed KMS.
[01:15] Ethan Patel: Got it. For the chat workload, can you approximate average tokens per request and typical prompt length?
[01:22] Liam Roberts: Avg 140 tokens in prompt, 80 tokens response, so about 220 tokens roundtrip. But some attachments bump it up.
[01:35] Maya Chen: So that gives us a burn estimate — quick calcs on the call, um, roughly 44k tokens per minute at 200 RPS? Let me not flub the math, Ethan?
[01:46] Ethan Patel: Yeah, with 200 RPS * 220 tokens ~ 44k tokens/sorry per second? wait — per second would be 44k tokens per second which is high; per minute we'd be 2.64M tokens. Right, so hourly matters. For billing and warmup we care about concurrency shapes.
[02:10] Liam Roberts: Right, we care about sustained bursts of 10-15 minutes during business hours. Nightly batch is more throughput oriented.
[02:20] Derek Cho: Security note — we cannot send PII off-region. So we need to validate Private or Dedicated in-region with customer-managed KMS, and audit logs for every request.
[02:34] Maya Chen: Understood. Let's walk through deployment options. Hosted is fastest to get started, Redwood hosted API — quick to prototype, but shared infra. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, capacity isolation. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives full control but adds ops overhead.
[02:56] Sofia Alvarez: How big of a difference in latency are we talking between hosted vs dedicated vs private if we use same model?
[03:02] Ethan Patel: If same model and same hardware class, Dedicated and Private are comparable. Hosted can have slightly higher variance due to multi-tenant routing — p95 maybe +30-50 ms on average. Biggest differences come from model variant and quantization choices.
[03:22] Liam Roberts: What about fallback strategies? If we lose capacity in Dedicated, can we route to hosted?
[03:27] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing can failover to a compatible hosted variant. We use policy-based routing — cost vs latency policies.
[03:36] Ethan Patel: For the POC, recommended approach: run initial benchmarks on Redwood hosted with the actual prompts to get baseline latency and token burn, then run a Dedicated config in-region (A100 GPUs) to validate throughput and deterministic latency. If you need on-prem due to compliance, plan a private deployment after we validate the workload.
[03:55] Sofia Alvarez: Sounds reasonable. Timeline?
[03:57] Maya Chen: We suggested 6 weeks — week 1: onboarding + data and SAML test account; week 2-3: baseline benchmarks on hosted and dedicated; week 4: security review for Private; week 5-6: final run and acceptance.
[04:16] Liam Roberts: Acceptance criteria — p95 < 300 ms for chat, nightly embedding job completes within SLA window (6 hours), SLA of 99.9% availability for inference endpoints for production.
[04:31] Ethan Patel: For the embedding job, quantization is helpful. We often use 4-bit int8-ish quant — the runtime supports q4_0 and q8 variants; you'll trade a tiny quality regression for a 2-3x cost improvement.
[04:48] Derek Cho: Can you send evals comparing quality across those quant levels? We need to show no regression on our test prompts.
[04:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include a small eval report.
[04:58] Sofia Alvarez: Networking — can Redwood support PrivateLink or direct VPC peering?
[05:03] Ethan Patel: Yes, for Dedicated we can set up VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on your cloud. For Private on-prem we'll do an air-gapped package or a customer-controlled VPC with our control plane. Sometimes names get swapped — "Redwood Dedikate" — but it's the same idea.
[05:19] Liam Roberts: What's the expected cost delta? Rough ballpark hosted vs dedicated vs private for our scale.
[05:24] Maya Chen: Ballpark: hosted is easiest but per-token unit cost highest; Dedicated has committed monthly base plus lower per-token; Private has higher initial setup and license/ops but lowest marginal cost at scale. We'll send a TCO example spreadsheet.
[05:40] Ethan Patel: Important for benchmarks: we need sample traffic trace and a 1k subset of real prompts. Please remove PII or obfuscate as needed. We can run both cold-start and warmed KV cache tests — the KV cache/prefix cache is huge for latency on conversational flows.
[05:58] Derek Cho: We'll sanitize and upload to S3 with a pre-signed link.
[06:02] Maya Chen: Great. On the metrics side we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 100k tokens. We'll also capture failure modes and tail latencies.
[06:18] Liam Roberts: For models — which families do you recommend? Our quality bar is high; we prefer an open model.
[06:24] Ethan Patel: We usually recommend an instruction-tuned 7B-13B family for chat as a starting point, then test a 70B quant variant if quality demands it. For embeddings use a smaller dedicated embed model unless you need semantic fidelity where larger helps. We'll propose 2 model candidates and variants for quantization.
[06:45] Liam Roberts: Any limitations on sequence length? We have docs up to 8k tokens sometimes.
[06:50] Ethan Patel: The runtime supports up to 32k with appropriate memory; the tradeoff is latency and memory per request. For long contexts we may shard or use retrieval-augmented patterns to keep token costs down.
[07:07] Sofia Alvarez: Audit logging — we need full request/response traces for legal. Retention 1 year. Is that supported?
[07:14] Maya Chen: Yes, both Dedicated and Private support extended log retention and integration to SIEMs. Hosted can also ship logs but may have constraints on retention length without add-on. We'll include logging retention options in the security docs.
[07:30] Derek Cho: KMS — can we bring our own key?
[07:33] Ethan Patel: Yes, customer-managed KMS supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK integrations in select regions.
[07:44] Liam Roberts: Ok. Decision criteria summary on our side: 1) In-region data control (must) 2) p95 latency under 300 ms (must) 3) predictable capacity during bursts (prefer dedicated) 4) acceptable cost metrics (prefer dedicated or private at scale).
[08:05] Maya Chen: Good, that maps cleanly to our recommendation: run POC baseline on hosted to get quick numbers, then dedicated in-region to validate latency and capacity, and evaluate private only if mandatory.
[08:18] Ethan Patel: Technical POC specifics: we'll test three configurations — hosted baseline, dedicated A100 80GB pool with autoscale to N GPUs, and a private VPC deployment (if requested). Benchmarks: steady-state 200 RPS with 220 tokens, 15-minute bursts, and nightly embedding throughput test. We'll produce a benchmark report with raw logs and proposed SLOs.
[08:45] Liam Roberts: That sounds good. Any blockers for onboarding?
[08:48] Maya Chen: Need SAML test account and sample prompts. Also access to whichever cloud region you want dedicated to run in.
[08:55] Derek Cho: We'll get IT to set up those things.
[08:58] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick Qs from the customer?
[09:01] Liam Roberts: What about rate limits and quotas on hosted during POC?
[09:04] Ethan Patel: We'll temporarily lift some quotas for the benchmark. For safety we set per-model QPS caps and throttles.
[09:12] Sofia Alvarez: Do you support RBAC so only certain Marigold users can call production models?
[09:16] Maya Chen: Yes, RBAC and token scoping. For Dedicated/Private you get full enterprise RBAC with SSO and SCIM provisioning.
[09:24] Liam Roberts: Great.
[09:26] Maya Chen: Okay let's close with explicit next steps and responsibilities.
[09:30] Ethan Patel: I'll own the benchmark runs and attach the raw logs.
[09:33] Maya Chen: I'll send pricing and security docs.
[09:36] Derek Cho: We'll upload sanitized prompts and set up SAML test account.
[09:40] Liam Roberts: And we'll aim to make the decision after the benchmark report, target end of February.
[09:46] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[09:48] Liam Roberts: Thanks.
